correctness.rationale: In the stated stationary-relative-coordinate dimer, the signed drift has zero quadratic covariation with X; the telegraph sign at jump instants can be replaced by its predictable left version without changing the integral against continuous X. Conditional on the entire Y and sign paths, B=∫S dW^x is standard Brownian motion with a conditional law independent of both paths. Hence the continuous entropy path has the representation c∫Y²ds−sqrt(2c)∫Y dB with c=2κ²/D and B independent of Y. Given Y, its mean path is c∫Y²ds and covariance at s,t is 2c∫_0^min(s,t)Y²du. This proves path-law invariance directly. The terminal Gaussian mixture gives the tilt u=−cq(1−q), the detailed symmetry and unit tilt normalization (including the degenerate T=0 case). With OU generator 2D∂²−2ky∂, the Gaussian ansatz yields A′=8DA²−4kA+u, B′=4DA; the stationary average inserts (1−2DA/k)^−1/2, yielding the stated denominator. For positive u in the stated open tilt interval, the OU covariance kernel (D/k)e^(−2k|s−t|) has operator norm at most D/k² by the row-integral bound, so the Gaussian quadratic moment is finite for u<k²/(2D); the transform extends from nonpositive u by analyticity. The leading hyperbolic exponential gives the asserted scaled transform. Wick covariance of Y² and total variance recover both cumulants. The velocity covariance decays at 2(k+λ), giving the stated strictly decreasing D_eff. The shipped numerical checker was inspected, not executed; its finite Riccati, quadrature and Gaussian-mixture tests do not establish the process law. No finite-time total-system entropy assertion is verified.

value.rationale: This is an exact identifiability obstruction for a natural observable in an established model. In the scope stated, even continuous observation of the entire medium-entropy path cannot distinguish flip rates, while the position variance growth can. The path result rules out recovery from entropy autocorrelations or higher moments as well as its mean, and the transform enables finite-time predictions. The stochastic rotation and OU transform are standard tools; the useful invariant is the resolved comparison of two observables in the same dynamics, not a new OU method or a claim about total entropy.
